We're doing an audit of several legacy marketing pixels on our site and need to confirm how Redwood's console and SDK treat signals coming from first-party vs third-party cookies, and what that implies for cross-border transfers under the DPA. A few concrete items: 

- If we drop a small legacy pixel that sends a hashed user ID and page path to your hosted telemetry endpoint, is that considered "personal data" under our DPA clauses when the data comes from an EU visitor?
- Do you (Redwood) ever persist raw identifiers (even hashed) outside the EU region by default for hosted customers, or is it explicitly kept within region when requested?
- We have older cookies with long TTLs (~1 year). Is there a recommended config in the console to limit retention or strip long-lived cookie values before ingestion?

I've attached a spreadsheet with the list of pixels and sample payloads (GreenLeaf_DPA_qa.xlsx). Legal asked if you can provide a short write-up we can add to our audit that lists: 1) whether these telemetry events are subject to SCCs/Special transfer mechanisms, 2) how subprocessors are involved, and 3) any console settings we should use to minimize transfer scope.

Can you point us to the right person or confirm details here? We're aiming to complete the audit by next Thursday (27 May).

Hi team — reviewed the sample payloads in the spreadsheet. High level answers (short) below; Olga will add the compliance specifics: 

- Default routing/region: For hosted customers we route ingestion to the region tied to the account by default. For EU accounts we can configure ingestion endpoints that keep raw payloads in eu-central-1. If you are on our hosted plan and haven't asked for EU-only, check the account metadata; we can apply EU pinning on request.
- Raw identifiers: We do not store plaintext identifiers outside the pinned region when EU-only is in effect. For non-pinned accounts, we may replicate metadata (anonymized counters, aggregated metrics) across regions for analytics, not raw payloads.
- TTL/Retention: Console has a "telemetry retention" dropdown per dataset (30/90/365/Custom). For legacy cookies with long TTLs we recommend: set ingestion rule to drop cookie value fields named cookie|uid|client_id and instead send a one-way hashed token that you rotate monthly. This reduces exposure and transfer scope.
- First vs Third party: The SDK/console tags events as first_party vs third_party based on the request origin and cookie domain in the sample payload. If a pixel is served from your domain, it's treated as first_party; if third-party domains are present, the signal is labeled third_party and may trigger additional privacy handling.

I've pasted a short snippet you can include in your audit below: 
"Redwood Inference treats telemetry as customer-controlled data. For EU accounts we support EU-pinned ingestion endpoints and do not export raw identifiers outside the pinned region. Customers may configure retention and field-stripping rules via the Console to limit cross-border transfers."

Link to the Console doc with the telemetry retention and field rules: https://docs.redwood.ai/telemetry/config#marketing-signals

Hi Anna — following up with the compliance details you requested. Apologies for the long note but trying to make it audit-ready.

1) Transfer legal basis: For hosted EU-pinned accounts we apply Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) for any onward transfer outside EEA that is strictly necessary (e.g., backup replication to a DR region). Our DPA includes those mechanisms and the signed DPA template has the SCC annex. If you are looking to avoid any cross-border transfer at all, we also offer Dedicated or Private deployment models (dedicated capacity or private VPC) where data never leaves customer-controlled regions per contract.

2) Subprocessors: We use a constrained set of subprocessors for telemetry ingestion and storage. The current list is in the attached PDF (requested_subprocessor_list_2027-05.pdf) and on the Drive link shared above. Notable subprocessors for telemetry: 
- Cloud object storage (eu-central-1): Data at rest encryption managed by Redwood (KMS).
- Indexing/search service: only aggregated indexes; raw payloads remain in storage.

3) Cookie / identifier handling guidance for audit text: 
- If the payload contains persistent cookie values or third-party partner identifiers, recommend that you either remove those fields pre-ingest or convert to a salt+hash that you rotate.
- TTL: Our recommended maximum retention for marketing signals used for attribution is 90 days. If your policy requires longer retention, we recommend documenting a business justification in your audit and noting that long-lived identifiers increase transfer scope.

4) Evidence snippet you can paste into your audit: 
"Redwood Inference (Controller/Processor as per DPA) supports EU-pinned ingestion endpoints. For pinned accounts, raw telemetry payloads are retained in the selected EU region and are not exported outside the EU except where contractually required and documented under SCCs. Subprocessor list and DPA templates are available on request (see attachments)."

Action items for GreenLeaf: please confirm the list of pixel domains and whether sample payloads include partner_id or third_party_id fields. Also let us know if you need a signed DPA with the SCC annex — I can route that to our legal ops.

Olga Petrov
